refs.quote: In patients with chronic renal impairment (creatinine clearance between 10 and 62 mL/min/1.73 m2), the disposition of omeprazole was very similar to that in healthy subjects, although there was a slight increase in bioavailability.

renal_basis.note: No dosage adjustment required; slight increase in bioavailability is not clinically meaningful.

Omeprazole belongs to a class of antisecretory compounds, the substituted benzimidazoles, that suppress gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.

mg_safety.note: Proton pump inhibitor; no neuromuscular junction blocking warnings.

value.instructions: Swallow delayed-release capsules whole; do not chew or crush enteric-coated pellets. For patients unable to swallow intact capsules, open capsule, empty pellets onto one tablespoon of cool soft applesauce, mix, and swallow immediately with cool water without chewing or crushing pellets.

refs.quote: Swallow omeprazole delayed-release capsules whole; do not chew. • For patients unable to swallow an intact capsule, omeprazole delayed-release capsules can be opened and administered as follows:

Swallow applesauce and pellets immediately with a glass of cool water to ensure complete swallowing of the pellets. Do not chew or crush the pellets. Do not save the applesauce and pellets for future use.

pgx.value: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers (~3% of Caucasians, 15% to 20% of Asians) have higher systemic exposure (AUC in Asian subjects ~4-fold higher than Caucasians). Dosage reduction to 10 mg once daily is recommended in Asian patients for maintenance of healing of erosive esophagitis.

refs.quote: Approximately 3% of Caucasians and 15 to 20% of Asians are CYP2C19 poor metabolizers. In a pharmacokinetic study of single 20 mg omeprazole dose, the AUC of omeprazole in Asian subjects was approximately four-fold of that in Caucasians
Dosage reduction of omeprazole to 10 mg once daily is recommended for Asian patients for maintenance of healing of EE

mechanism_of_action.value: Substituted benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor that suppresses gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell, blocking the final step of acid production.

refs.quote: Omeprazole belongs to a class of antisecretory compounds, the substituted benzimidazoles, that suppress gastric acid secretion by specific inhibition of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.
Omeprazole is a time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C19, resulting in autoinhibition and nonlinear pharmacokinetics.

The major part of its metabolism is dependent on the polymorphically expressed CYP2C19, responsible for the formation of hydroxyomeprazole, the major metabolite in plasma. The remaining part is dependent on another specific isoform, CYP3A4, responsible for the formation of omeprazole sulphone.

enzyme_profile.note: Also a major substrate of CYP2C19 (time-dependent autoinhibitor of CYP2C19) and substrate of CYP3A4.

value.effect: Decreased exposure of rilpivirine (AUC -40%, Cmax -40%, Cmin -33%), reducing antiviral effect and promoting drug resistance.
value.management: Concomitant use with omeprazole is contraindicated.

refs.quote: Rilpivirine-containing products: Concomitant use with omeprazole is contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ].

value.effect: Reduced plasma concentrations of active metabolite of clopidogrel (by 41-46%) and reduced platelet inhibition.
value.management: Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole; consider alternative antiplatelet therapy.

refs.quote: Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole. Consider use of alternative anti-platelet therapy [see Warnings and Precautions (5.7) ].

value.effect: Markedly decreased antiretroviral exposure (atazanavir AUC -94%, nelfinavir AUC -36%), reducing antiviral efficacy.

refs.quote: Atazanavir: Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole. See prescribing information for atazanavir for dosing information. Nelfinavir: Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole.

value.effect: Increased saquinavir exposure (AUC +82%, Cmax +75%, Cmin +106%), increasing toxicity.
value.management: Monitor clinically and with laboratory tests for saquinavir-related toxicities.

refs.quote: Therefore, clinical and laboratory monitoring for saquinavir toxicity is recommended during concurrent use with omeprazole.

value.effect: Increased INR and prothrombin time, which may lead to abnormal bleeding and death.
value.management: Monitor INR and prothrombin time and adjust warfarin dose if needed.

refs.quote: Monitor INR and prothrombin time and adjust the dose of warfarin, if needed, to maintain target INR range.

value.effect: May elevate and prolong serum concentrations of methotrexate and/or hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities.
value.management: Consider temporary withdrawal of omeprazole in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.

refs.quote: A temporary withdrawal of omeprazole may be considered in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.

value.effect: Increased exposure of citalopram leading to an increased risk of QT prolongation.
value.management: Limit the dose of citalopram to a maximum of 20 mg per day.

refs.quote: Increased exposure of citalopram leading to an increased risk of QT prolongation [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ]. Intervention: Limit the dose of citalopram to a maximum of 20 mg per day.

value.effect: Increased exposure of cilostazol and its active metabolite 3,4-dihydro-cilostazol.
value.management: Reduce the dose of cilostazol to 50 mg twice daily.

refs.quote: Reduce the dose of cilostazol to 50 mg twice daily. See prescribing information for cilostazol.

value.effect: Potential for increased exposure of phenytoin via CYP2C19 inhibition.
value.management: Monitor phenytoin serum concentrations; dose adjustment may be needed.

refs.quote: Monitor phenytoin serum concentrations. Dose adjustment may be needed to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations.

value.effect: Increased exposure of diazepam (27% decreased clearance, 36% longer half-life).
value.management: Monitor patients for increased sedation and reduce diazepam dose as needed.

refs.quote: Monitor patients for increased sedation and reduce the dose of diazepam as needed.

value.effect: Potential for increased exposure of digoxin (bioavailability +10%).
value.management: Monitor digoxin concentrations; dose adjustment may be needed.

refs.quote: Monitor digoxin concentrations. Dose adjustment may be needed to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations.

value.drug_or_class: Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) and Drugs Dependent on Gastric pH
value.effect: Reduced absorption/exposure (MPA Cmax -52%, AUC -23%) due to increased gastric pH.
value.management: Use omeprazole with caution in transplant patients receiving MMF.

refs.quote: Use omeprazole with caution in transplant patients receiving MMF [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ].

value.effect: Potential for increased exposure of tacrolimus, especially in CYP2C19 intermediate or poor metabolizers.
value.management: Monitor tacrolimus whole blood concentrations and adjust dose if needed.

refs.quote: Monitor tacrolimus whole blood concentrations. Dose adjustment may be needed to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations.

value.management: Avoid concomitant use of St. John's Wort or rifampin with omeprazole.

tier.note: Large epidemiologic cohorts (Sweden n=955, Denmark n=1,800 first-trimester exposures) fail to demonstrate an increased risk of major congenital malformations (2.9% vs 2.6%), though no adequate well-controlled studies exist and animal studies showed dose-dependent embryo-lethality at 3.4-34x the 40 mg human dose.

refs.quote: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies with omeprazole in pregnant women. Available epidemiologic data fail to demonstrate an increased risk of major congenital malformations or other adverse pregnancy outcomes with first trimester omeprazole use.

Reproduction studies in rats and rabbits resulted in dose-dependent embryo-lethality at omeprazole doses that were approximately 3.4 to 34 times an oral human dose of 40 mg (based on a body surface area for a 60 kg person).
